title: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, State Commission and National Commission) Rules, 2021
authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
summary: These rules fix pecuniary jurisdiction under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: District Commission for claims up to ₹50 lakh; State Commission for claims above ₹50 lakh up to ₹2 crore; National Commission for claims above ₹2 crore.
text:
Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021 — pecuniary jurisdiction:

District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission: complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed ₹50 lakh.

State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission: complaints where the consideration exceeds ₹50 lakh but does not exceed ₹2 crore.

National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission: complaints where the consideration exceeds ₹2 crore.

'Value' for jurisdiction is determined as prescribed under the 2019 Act and these rules (verify the current position — slabs have been revised in the past). Appeals from the District Commission lie to the State Commission within the limitation period prescribed by the Act, and from the State Commission to the National Commission.

Filing: complaints can be filed physically or online (e-Daakhil portal) from anywhere in India in terms of the 2019 Act's flexible venue provisions.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — condensed summary for demonstration purposes. Verify the current slabs at consumeraffairs.nic.in before relying on it.

title: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 — procedure
instrument: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
summary: These rules govern the procedure of consumer commissions: complaint contents, admission scrutiny, notice to the opposite party, written reply timelines, evidence by affidavit, and e-filing through e-Daakhil.
text:
Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 — procedure highlights:

Complaint contents: the complaint should set out the facts, the deficiency alleged, the relief sought, and be accompanied by evidence (invoice, warranty, correspondence) and an affidavit verifying the facts.

On admission, the commission issues notice to the opposite party; the opposite party must submit a written version within the time allowed (commonly 30 days, extendable as per the rules) and may deny or justify the deficiency.

Evidence of parties is ordinarily by affidavit; the commission may allow cross-examination where required. Commissions are empowered to order interim relief in appropriate cases.

E-filing: complaints, replies, and documents can be filed through the e-Daakhil portal including from locations outside the commission's territorial limits as permitted under the Act.

Fees: filing fee slabs by claim value are prescribed under the rules (verify the current schedule on the consumeraffairs.nic.in portal before filing).

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — condensed summary for demonstration purposes. Verify the current rules at consumeraffairs.nic.in before relying on it.
